children: on Wednesday announced that it succeeded in a mid-stage trial for tulisokibart, its experimental therapy for an inflammatory skin condition known as hidradenitis suppurativa, positioning the antibody drug for late-stage development.

Citing data from its Phase 2b trial MK-7240-012, the company said that the anti-TL1A monoclonal antibody at both high and medium doses reached the study’s main goal in terms of Hidradenitis Suppurativa Clinical Response 50 (HiSCR50).
, 72% and 64% of patients in the high-dose and medium-dose groups achieved HiSCR50, implying a 37% and 29% improvement over the placebo group in 16 weeks, respectively.

Regarding tolerability, the company said that the rate of adverse events in patients who received high-, medium-, and low doses stood at 42.9%, 47.6%, and 52.4%, respectively, compared with 40.9% in the off-drug arm.

The rates of serious adverse events reached 2.4% in both the high- and medium-dose groups compared with 4.8% in the low-dose group and 2.3% with placebo. The company said that the data will inform its late-stage development program
Characterized by painful nodules and abscesses, HS affects an estimated 1 in 100 people globally in a market served by companies such as AbbVie
with their FDA-approved therapies, Humira and Cosentyx, respectively.

title: Merck succeeds in mid-stage trial for skin disease drug
